title: Dispatch TUR 2: A Timetable for a Railway Without Rails
summary: An Eidetician finds that the postmarks follow a journey no train has made.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The impossible letters are arriving in the order of a printed timetable. Archivist and Eidetician Dr. Lenora Saye has compared their cancellation times with the proposed Westmere schedule of 1881. Every letter was posted before the departure of a 6:40 evening service from Kingsfen and sorted during its supposed journey toward Alderwick.

The printed schedule is more than an old curiosity. Surveyors of the period used it to calculate which sections of embankment must be raised first. The company printed thousands of copies to attract investors before its charter failed. Dr. Saye suggests that such a detailed account of a journey never taken may have left an unusually stable course in the Eidetic Stratum.

Mr. Pike objects to that explanation. His staff has found ordinary dust, wet ink, and a trace of coal grit on the envelopes. “I have a sack of post,” he said, “not a philosophical argument.” The sack now contains thirty-seven letters. Some name passengers expected to board the service in October 1894; others ask relatives to meet it.

Mrs. Harrow received a second letter from Miriam yesterday. The child describes sharing a seat with a boy called Theo and asks whether the lamps on Alderwick’s platform are still red. There is no Alderwick platform. The 1881 plan ended the railway at a field behind the old goods depot.

Dr. Saye has requested access to that field and to the company’s original timetable plate. The plate was sold after the charter failed. Its present owner, retired engineer Gideon Wren, has agreed to bring it to the Eidetical Institute tomorrow.
